ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r6.claim: Saḥt literally means peeling meat from a bone and by extension exploitation or uprooting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r6.anchor: is to peel off meat from a bone

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r7.claim: Moses delivers this speech first in the contest arena before the gathering.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r7.anchor: This is the speech which Moses (sws) delivered foremost

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r8.claim: The expression about imputing falsehood to God refers to polytheism, in a debate over Pharaoh's claim to divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r8.anchor: refers to polytheism as has been explained

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r9.claim: Moses had refuted Pharaoh's claim by saying the true Lord created and sustains the universe, unlike Pharaoh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p45/r9.anchor: the real debate with the Pharaoh was that

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r1.claim: The partners attributed to God have no revealed proof and are fabrications, making those who invent them liable to punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r1.anchor: revealed any proof in their favour

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r2.claim: This false attribution makes them worthy of punishment and is the fate of wrongdoers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p46/r2.anchor: made them worthy of his punishment

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r2.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص، والأعمش، وطلحة، وابن جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r2.claim: These readers say فيسحتكم with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ, from the quadriliteral verb أسحت.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص والأعمش وطلحة وابن جرير فيسحتكم بضم الياء وكسر الحاء من أسحت رباعيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r3.speaker: باقي السبعة، ورويس، وابن عباعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r3.claim: The remaining canonical readers, Ruways, and Ibn Abāʿī read فيسحتكم with both vowels open, from the triliteral سحت.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p349/r3.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة ورويس وابن عباعي بفتحهما من سحت ثلاثيا

NAHHAS:v3p41/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r19.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p41/r19.claim: Abu Ishaq reads waylan as a verbal noun meaning that God imposed woe on them, and also allows it as an annexed vocative.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r19.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق أي ألزمهم الله جل وعز ويلا قال ويجوز أن يكون نداءا مضافا

NAHHAS:v3p41/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p41/r20.claim: Faysḥitkum answers the prohibition; the Kufans read faysḥitkum, while the Hijazi form is preferable and the latter is Tamimi.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r20.anchor: فيستحكم بعذاب ) جواب النهي وقرأ الكوفيون ( فيسحتكم ) والأولى لغة أهل الحجاز وهذه لغة بني تميم

NAHHAS:v3p41/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r21.speaker: الفرزدق
NAHHAS:v3p41/r21.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line with masḥatan is evidence for the Tamimi reading.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r21.anchor:
قال الفرزدق
( وعض زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع … من المال إلا مسحتا أو مجلف

NAHHAS:v3p41/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p41/r22.claim: The warning means they must not falsely call the proofs Moses brings sorcery; whoever invents lies has lost mercy and reward.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r22.anchor: ومعنى لا تفتروا على الله كذبا لا تقولوا إن الذي أجيء به من البراهين سحر ( وقد خاب من افترى ) أي

TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r8.claim: 'Wayl' is a threat of punishment; 'may God punish you' expresses the phrase's original sense.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r8.anchor: الويل كلمة عذاب وتهديد، والأصل فيه معنى العذاب

TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r9.claim: 'Saḥt' means complete removal, associated with shaving hair; 'isḥāt' means eradication and destruction.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r9.anchor: والسحت بفتح السين استيصال لشعر بالحلق والإسحات الإستئصال والإهلاك

TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r10.claim: The plural address covers Pharaoh, his schemes, magicians, and other helpers; it cannot refer only to magicians, who were not previously mentioned.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r10.anchor: ضمائر الجمع غيبة وخطابا لفرعون وكيده وهم السحرة وسائر أعوانه على موسى

TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r11.claim: Moses warns them not to attribute falsehood to God; Pharaoh's labeling miracles as magic and the mission as political intrigue severs those claims from God, as does magic presented as mere magic.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#6/r11.anchor: إنما يكون بنسبة ما ليس من الله إليه

TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r1.claim: The magicians sought reward for winning, and Pharaoh promised both payment and close status; inducements or threats made them face Moses.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r1.anchor: أئن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r1.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، حفص عن عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai and Hafs from Asim read يُسحتكم with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ, from quadriliteral أسحت in Najd and Tamim; the others use triliteral سحت in Hijaz.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان وحفص عن عصام " فيسحتكم " بضم الياء وكسر الحاء. والباقون بفتحهما

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r2.claim: The root conveys exhaustive removal and depletion, hence destruction or doing away.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r2.anchor: وأصل هذه المادة الدلالة على الاستقصاء والنفاد

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq al-Tamimi's مسحتا illustrates the dialectal form.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r3.anchor: وعض زمان يا بن مروان لم يدع من المال إلا مسحتا أو مجلف

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r4.claim: فيسحتكم is accusative with an elided أن as the response to the prohibition لا تفتروا.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r4.anchor: ونصبه بإضمار " أن " في جواب النهي

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r5.claim: In the first poetic transmission, مسحتا is understood as the quasi-subject of “nothing remained,” so raised مجلف is coordinated with it; Zamakhshari cites this for raised قليل at 2:249.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r5.anchor: أن معنى لم يدع من المال إلا مسحتا: لم يبق إلا مسحت

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r6.claim: A second parse raises مجلف by an omitted verb understood from لم يدع: أو بقي مجلف.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r6.anchor: مرفوع بفعل مقدر دل عليه لم يدع، والتقدير: أو بقي مجلف

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r7.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ parses مجلف as a subject with an omitted predicate, estimated as أو مجلف كذلك.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r7.anchor: مجلف " مبتدأ، وخبره مضمر تقديره: أو مجلف كذلك وهو تخريج الفراء

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r8.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r8.claim: Al-Kisai coordinates مجلف with the hidden pronoun in مسحتا; although separation is normally expected, he does not require it, and poetry permits it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r8.anchor: لا يشترط وهو الكسائي. وأيضا فهو جائز في الضرورة عند الكل

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r9.claim: Al-Farisi treats مجلف as a verbal noun on the pattern of a passive participle, as in ممزق at 34:19, and coordinates it with عض زمان.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r9.anchor: الخامس: أن يكون " مجلف " مصدرا بزنة اسم المفعول كقوله تعالى: كل ممزق

SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r10.claim: The author prefers the fifth, al-Farisi's verbal-noun analysis of مجلف.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61/r10.anchor: وهو قول الفارسي. وهو عندي أحسنها

SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r1.claim: A second transmission has dāl kasra and raised مسحت as subject of ودع “remain,” with مجلف coordinated and an omitted pronoun meaning “because of it.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r1.anchor: الرواية الثانية: فتح الياء وكسر الدال ورفع مسحت. وتخريجها واضح

SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r2.claim: A third transmission makes يدع passive with مسحت as its نائب فاعل and مجلف coordinated.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r2.anchor: الرواية الثالثة: " يدع " بضم الياء وفتح الدال على ما لم يسم فاعله، و " مسحت " بالرفع

SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r3.claim: In the passive form, the wāw should remain because it is not between yāʾ and kasra; its deletion is analogical to the active form. The fuller discussion is referred to under al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:20:61#2/r3.anchor: وكان من حق الواو أن لا تحذف، بل تثبت لأنها لم تقع بين ياء وكسرة

ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r1.claim: ويلكم may be accusative under an understood verb, as if God imposed woe on them, or accusative as a vocative, like 19:4 and 36:52.
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r1.anchor: ويلكم) منصوب على أن ألزمهم الله ويلا، ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على النداء

ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r2.claim: فيسحتكم is also read with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ; سحته and أسحته both mean to eradicate and destroy.
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r2.anchor: ويقرأ (فيسحتكم) - بضم الياء وكسر الحاء، يقال سحته، وأسحته إذا استأصله

ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r3.speaker: الفرزدق
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq's مسحتا illustrates the form derived from أسحت meaning eradicated; the more common transmission of his verse also has مسحتا.
ZAJJAJ:v3p360#2/r3.anchor: قال الفرزدق: وعض زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع. . . من المال إلا مسحتا أو مجلف

ASAD-NOTES:20:61/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:61/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:61/r1.claim: Moses warns them not to invent lies against God, lest grievous suffering strike them; a fabricator is already doomed.
ASAD-NOTES:20:61/r1.anchor: Woe unto you! Do not invent lies against God, [43] lest He afflict you

ASAD-NOTES:20:61#n43/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:61#n43/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:61#n43/r1.claim: Inventing lies against God means deliberately denying the truth of His messages.
ASAD-NOTES:20:61#n43/r1.anchor: by deliberately denying the truth of His messages

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم برواية أبي بكر وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Bakr's narration from Asim, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read the verb with initial fatḥa, from يسحت.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: (فيسحتكم) بفتح الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r2.claim: Hafs from Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read with initial ḍamma and a kasra on ḥāʾ, from أسحت.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية حفص وحمزة والكسائي: فيسحتكم بضم الياء من أسحت، وكسر الحاء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses يسحتكم as destroying you and says Banu Tamim also use يسحتكم; a poetic use of مسحت supports the sense of stripping away or leaving nothing.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r3.anchor: أبو عبيدة: يسحتكم: يهلككم قال: وبنو تميم يقولون: يسحتكم، وأنشد

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن وأبو عثمان
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r4.claim: Abu al-Hasan gives the same explanation, and Abu Uthman says saḥata and asḥata are equivalent, agreeing with Abu Ubayda.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p228/r4.anchor: وفسر لم يدع: لم يبق، وقال أبو الحسن نحو ذلك، أبو عثمان: سحت وأسحت نحو قول أبي عبيدة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p242/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p242/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p242/r1.claim: The verb has two dialectal readings: fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ from saḥata, or ḍamma and kasra from asḥata; both mean to destroy utterly.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p242/r1.anchor: يقرأبفتح الياء والحاء وبضم الياء وكسر الحاء وهما لغتان

QIRAAT-ER:20:61:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:61:12#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:20:61:12#1/r1.claim: Form I yasḥata means God directly scrapes or destroys them, while standard Form IV yusḥita means He causes their destruction, implying intermediation.
QIRAAT-ER:20:61:12#1/r1.anchor: Vr, mutawatir: "Form I (saḥata) vs standard Form IV (asḥata) — yasḥata (I) = ""He scrapes/destroys you

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18/r1.claim: Qatada explains the threatened punishment as one that eradicates and destroys them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فيسحتكم بعذاب ﴾ قال فيستأصلكم فيهلككم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r3.claim: سحت is used in the Hijaz and أسحت in Najd and Tamim; its original sense is shaving hair completely, later extended to destruction and removal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r3.anchor: سحت: لغة الحجاز وأسحت لغة نجد وتميم، وأصله استقصاء الحلق للشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r4.claim: Failure means not attaining what one sought.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r1.claim: The text omits the mention of Moses arriving because his arrival is already established and needs no explicit statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r1.anchor: للايذان أنه أمر محقق غنى عن التصريح به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r2.claim: The sentence is a fresh explanatory start answering the implicit question of what Moses did when Pharaoh assembled the sorcerers; Moses addresses them as a warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r2.anchor: والجملة مستانفة استئنافا بيانيا كأنه قيل : فماذا صنع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r3.claim: Moses warns them not to claim that the signs soon shown through him are magic, as Pharaoh had done.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r3.anchor: بأن تدعوا إياته التى ستظهر على يدى سحرا كما فعل فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r4.claim: The verb means that God will utterly destroy them with a terrible punishment beyond measure.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r4.anchor: هائل لا يقادر قدره وقرأ جماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r5.speaker: جماعة من السبعة وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r5.claim: A group among the Seven and Ibn ʿAbbās read the verb with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ, using the Hijazi triliteral form; the Najdi and Tamimi dialect uses the quadriliteral form isḥāt.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ جماعة من السبعة وابن عباس ( فيسحتكم ( بفتح الياء والحلق من الثلاثى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r6.claim: The warning generalizes: whoever fabricates a lie against God, in any manner, has failed, especially the fabrication Moses forbids.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r6.anchor: كائنا من كان باى وجه كان فيدخل فيه الأفتراء المنهى عنه دخولا أوليا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, the failed fabricator is Pharaoh, and Moses warns the sorcerers not to share his failure and frustration.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r7.anchor: أو قد خاب فرعون المفترى فلا تكونوا مثله فى الخيبة وعدم نجح الطلبة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r8.claim: The final clause is parenthetical and reinforces the preceding warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p220#3/r8.anchor: والجملة اعتراض مقرر لمضمون ما قبلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r2.claim: Moses addressed Pharaoh's sorcerers; one report gives 72, each with a rope and staff.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r2.anchor: قال لهم موسى} يعني: للسحرة الذين جمعهم فرعون، وكانوا اثنين وسبعين ساحرا، مع كل واحد حبل وعصا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r3.claim: Another report says there were 400 sorcerers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r4.speaker: كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r4.claim: Kaʿb says there were 12,000, or more.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r4.anchor: وقال كعب: كانوا اثني عشر ألفا. وقيل أكثر من ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص والباقون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r5.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ; others read with fatḥa; both are Arabic forms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r5.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص: {فيسحتكم} بضم الياء وكسر الحاء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r6.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r6.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī gloss the verb as destroying you.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r7.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses it as eradicating you completely.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p280/r8.claim: Whoever fabricates a lie has failed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r3.claim: Moses warns them not to falsely call God's signs sorcery.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r3.anchor: بأن تدعوا آياته سحرا. { فيسحتكم بعذاب } فيهلككم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r4.claim: The punishment will destroy and eradicate them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r4.anchor: فيهلككم ويستأصلكم، وبه قرأ حمزة والكسائي

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r5.claim: They read the verb with ḍamma, from isḥāt, a Najdi and Tamimi form; suḥt is the Hijazi form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r5.anchor: وبه قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص ويعقوب بالضم من الاسحات

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r6.claim: The fabricator fails, as Pharaoh did: his fabrication and scheming could not preserve his rule.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:60-63/r6.anchor: كما خاب فرعون، فإنه افترى واحتال ليبقى الملك عليه فلم ينفعه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r1.claim: Moses warns them not to invent claims against God by calling His established signs unreal magic, presenting illusion as truth, or associating partners with Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r1.anchor: لا تتعمدوا أن تصنعوا استعلاء { على الله كذبا } بحعلكم آياته العظام الثابتة سحرا لا حقيقة له

BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r2.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi says the root sense of يسحت is to exterminate completely.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r2.anchor: قال الرازي . وأصله الاستئصال { بعذاب } أي عظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r3.claim: Anyone who deliberately lies against God or anyone else is disappointed and ruined.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r3.anchor: كل { من افترى * } اي تعمد كذبا على الله أو على غيره

BURSEVI:v5p307/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p307/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p307/r4.claim: The wording answers the implied question of what Moses did when Pharaoh arrived with the magicians: he spoke to them as an adviser.
BURSEVI:v5p307/r4.anchor: كأنه قيل فماذا صنع موسى عند إتيان فرعون مع السحرة فقيل قال لهم بطريق النصيحة

BURSEVI:v5p307/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p307/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p307/r5.claim: Wailukum originally invokes ruin, as if saying may God bind you to misery; here it rebukes and restrains, urging them to stop fabricating.
BURSEVI:v5p307/r5.anchor: أصله الدعاء بالهلاك بمعنى ألزمكم الله ويلا يعني عذابا وهلاكا والمراد هنا الزجر والردع

BURSEVI:v5p307/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p307/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p307/r6.claim: Moses warns them not to claim falsely that the coming signs are magic, and not to associate partners with God; iftirāʾ is deliberate falsehood.
BURSEVI:v5p307/r6.anchor: بأن تدعو أن الآيات التي ستظهر على يدي سحر أو لا تشركوا مع الله أحدا والافتراء التقول والكذب عن عمد

BURSEVI:v5p307/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p307/r7.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v5p307/r7.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt specifies the warning: do not perform magic under the guise of a miracle, falsely claiming God gave you what He gave the prophets.
BURSEVI:v5p307/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : قال موسى للسحرة {ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا}

BURSEVI:v5p307/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p307/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p307/r8.claim: Yusḥitkum means that God will annihilate and uproot them through the torment.

BURSEVI:v5p307/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p307/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p307/r9.claim: The threatened torment is immense and beyond measure.

BURSEVI:v5p307/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p307/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p307/r10.claim: Khayba is missing one’s aim; anyone who invents a lie against God, whoever they are and however they do it, will fail.
BURSEVI:v5p307/r10.anchor: الخيبة فوت المطلب أي : (بى بهره ونا اميدماند) {من افترى}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p247/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p247/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p247/r10.claim: “Moses said to them” begins an explanatory sentence: Pharaoh's arrival naturally raises the question of what happened next, and Moses opens by admonishing the magicians.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p247/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p247/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p247/r11.claim: “Them” may refer to the magicians implied by the promised matching magic, or to everyone present, since Pharaoh and his court could see and hear; the latter is implied by the gathered men of Pharaoh's scheme.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p247/r11.anchor: عائد إلى معلوم من قوله { فلنأتينك بسحر مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r1.claim: If “woe to you” is a genuine imprecation, Moses may be addressing only the magicians, not Pharaoh, so he does not violate the command to speak gently to Pharaoh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون أراد به حقيقة الدعاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r2.claim: Alternatively, after seeing that gentleness did not soften Pharaoh's settled disbelief, Moses may have been specially permitted to speak harshly, restricting the general command of gentleness, as Muhammad was permitted to fight in 22:39.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r2.anchor: أغلظ القول زجرا له بأمر خاص من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r3.claim: Alternatively, seeing the magicians mislead the crowd by invoking Pharaoh's might as proof of divine support, Moses regarded forceful verbal repudiation as the fitting way to oppose wrong.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r3.anchor: رأى واجبا عليه تغيير المنكر بلسانه بأقصى ما يستطيع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r4.claim: The word may instead express astonishment at a strange state, meaning “I marvel at you and warn you”; the Prophet used a similar expression to Abū Baṣīr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r4.anchor: مستعملة في التعجب من حال غريبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r5.claim: The Prophet called Abū Baṣīr “a fire-stirrer of war,” an expression Ibn ʿĀshūr cites as an example of astonished exclamation; no grading is given.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r5.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي بصير : ( ويل أمه مسعر حرب )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r6.claim: Wayl names punishment or evil and has no verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r6.anchor: اسم للعذاب والشر ، وليس له فعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r7.claim: “Waylakum” may be accusative with an omitted warning or exhortation verb, or with an omitted vocative particle, as in “O woe to us”; see 2:79.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r7.anchor: على إضمار فعل على التحذير أو الإغراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r8.claim: Iftirāʾ means fabricating a lie; combining it with “a lie” adds emphasis, as at 5:103.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r8.anchor: اختلاق الكذب . والجمع بينه وبين كذبا } للتأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r9.claim: Moses calls their sorcery a fabrication: they make ropes seem like snakes, claim divine backing, call Moses a liar and magician, or deify Pharaoh and his gods; their blasphemous claims varied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r9.anchor: والافتراء الذي عناه موسى هو ما يخيلونه للناس من الشعوذة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r10.claim: The warning against attributing lies to God is reinforced by 5:103, which describes disbelievers inventing falsehood about God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p248/r10.anchor: يفترون على الله الكذب في سورة المائدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r1.claim: The majority read yashaṭkum with fatḥa on yāʾ, from saḥata, “uproot”; this is the Hijazi dialect.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم وخلف ورويس عن يعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r2.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, Khalaf, and Ruways from Yaʿqūb read yusḥitkum with ḍamma on yāʾ, from asḥata, the Najdi and Tamimi dialect; both readings are eloquent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r2.anchor: حمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف ، ورويس عن يعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r3.claim: “Whoever fabricates has failed” is circumstantial to the prohibition and supplies its rationale: earlier fabricators failed to achieve their aim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r3.anchor: في موضع الحال من ضمير { لا تفتروا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r4.claim: The relative pronoun man is general: whoever fabricates.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r5.claim: The argument functions as the major premise of a categorical syllogism.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r5.anchor: وموقع هذه الجملة بعد التي قبلها كموقع القضية الكبرى من القياس الاقتراني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r6.claim: Moses signals that he would not falsely claim revelation: knowing that God would destroy him and that fabricators fail, he would not undertake such a lie.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p250/r6.anchor: وفي كلام موسى إعلان بأنه لا يتقول على الله ما لم يأمره به لأنه يعلم أنه يستأصله بعذاب ويعلم خيبة من افترى على الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.claim: Moses urges the sorcerers to tell the truth when they recognize it and not knowingly oppose it with lies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r3.anchor: وهذه مخاطبة محذرة ندبهم في هذه الآية إلى قول الحق إذا رأوه وأن لا يباهتوا بكذب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.claim: These readers use fatḥa on the initial yāʾ; the form means to destroy or remove.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر «فيسحتكم» بفتح الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.claim: These readers use ḍamma on the initial yāʾ; it is a dialectal form with the same meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم «فيسحتكم» بضم الياء وهما لغتان بمعنى يقال سحت وأسحت إذا أهلك وأذهب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.claim: Both forms mean destroy or remove; al-Farazdaq's line attests the form from asḥata.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p49#2/r6.anchor: فهذا من أسحت فلما سمع السحرة هذه المقالة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r1.claim: Moses addressed the sorcerers; their number was discussed earlier under al-Aʿrāf 114.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r1.anchor: قال لهم موسى أي للسحرة وقد ذكرنا عددهم في الأعراف 114

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses waylakum as an accusative governed by an understood verb, ‘May God bind you to woe.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج هو منصوب على ألزمكم الله ويلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, waylakum is a vocative, as in the phrase ‘O woe to us, who has raised us from our resting place?’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على النداء كقوله تعالى يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا يس 52

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the prohibition as a command not to associate anyone with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس لا تشركوا معه احدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r5.claim: These readers pronounce the yāʾ in yusḥitakum with fatḥa, from saḥata.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وابو بكر عن عاصم فيسحتكم بفتح الياء من سحت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r6.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from Asim pronounce the yāʾ with damma, from asḥata.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم فيسحتكم بضم الياء من أسحت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the form yusḥitu is more common and means extermination; Arabs use both saḥata and asḥata.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r7.anchor: قال الفراء ويسحت أكثر وهو الاستئصال والعرب تقول سحته الله وأسحته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r8.speaker: الفرزدق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r8.claim: Al-Farazdaq's verse uses masḥatan or masḥat to describe what remains of wealth after it has been consumed; Abu Ubayda reports the latter with nominative case.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p295#2/r8.anchor: قال الفرزدقز وعض زمان يا بن مروان لم يدع من المال إلا مسحتا أو مجلف هكذا أنشد البيت الفراء والزجاج ورواه أبو عبيدة الا مسحت أو مجلف بالرفع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r3.claim: Moses warns the magicians not to deceive people into thinking their illusions create real things, thereby falsely attributing creation to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r3.anchor: أي: لا تخيلوا للناس بأعمالكم إيجاد أشياء لا حقائق لها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r4.claim: The punishment threatened by Moses is annihilation without remainder.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r4.anchor: أي: يهلككم بعقوبة هلاكا لا بقية له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p300/r5.claim: Moses adds that anyone who fabricates a lie against God has failed.

JISHUMI:v7p4683/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r1.claim: Moses' challenge showed the distinction between a miracle and sleight of hand; another view says the magicians were numerous.
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r1.anchor: بين المعجز وبين الشعبذة، وقيل: كانوا ذا عدد كثير.

JISHUMI:v7p4683/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r2.claim: Denying the truth after proof and witnessing a miracle is graver and merits greater punishment.
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r2.anchor: تدل الآية أن التكذيب بعد إقامة الحجة ورؤية المعجز أعظم، والعقوبة عليها أكبر.

JISHUMI:v7p4683/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r3.claim: Human acts arise from people: otherwise God's signs, attribution of turning away and denial to them, and punishment for those acts would make no sense.
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن أفعال العباد حادثة من جهتهم؛ إذ لو كانت خلقا لله تعالى لما اعتبر الآيات

JISHUMI:v7p4683/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r4.claim: The challenge was scheduled in daylight with everyone gathered, demonstrating a public miracle; sleight of hand works on individuals or the ignorant, often secretly at night.
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r4.anchor: وهذا غاية المعجز؛ لأن الشعبذة إنما تنفذ على أفرادهم وجهالهم، وربما آثروه خفية وليلا

JISHUMI:v7p4683/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r5.claim: They read فيسحتكم with a damma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ.
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r5.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: فيسحتكم بضم الياء وكسر الحاء

JISHUMI:v7p4683/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r6.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r6.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa on both letters; both forms are dialect variants of سحت and أسحت.
JISHUMI:v7p4683/r6.anchor: والباقون بفتح الياء والحاء، وهما لغتان، سحت وأسحت.

JISHUMI:v7p4689/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r1.claim: خاب means he lost, was cut off, and was deprived of God’s reward for lying about God.
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r1.anchor: خسر وانقطع وجازه عن ثواب الله تعالى من كذب عليه، قاله موسى عظة وتخويفا

JISHUMI:v7p4689/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r2.claim: Moses spoke the warning as admonition and intimidation.
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r2.anchor: من كذب عليه، قاله موسى عظة وتخويفا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r1.claim: Mūsā warns them not to falsely call God's signs and miracles sorcery.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r1.anchor: أي لا تدعو آياته ومعجزاته سحرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r2.claim: A reading is noted for فيسحتكم; سحت is the Hijazi form, while إسحات is used in Najd and by Banū Tamīm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r2.anchor: قرىء { فيسحتكم } والسحت لغة أهل الحجاز . والإسحات : لغة أهل نجد وبني تميم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r3.speaker: الفرزدق
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq's fragment إلا مسحتا أو مجلف is cited as evidence for the regional word form; the source notes a grammatical dispute over parsing its verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p73#2/r3.anchor:
ومنه قول الفرزدق :
. . . . . . إلا مسحتا أو مجلف ;

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r1.claim: Moses warns the magicians not to falsely attribute their magic to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r1.anchor: لا تفتروا على الله كذبا بسحركم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r2.claim: Alternatively, he warns them not to call his message magic and thereby deny him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r2.anchor: الثاني : بتكذيبي وقولكم م جئت به سحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r3.claim: “He will utterly destroy you” means He will annihilate and uproot you.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r4.claim: Al-Farazdaq's verse uses “musaḥḥat” for what is uprooted, and “mujlaf” for what is destroyed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p409/r4.anchor: وعض زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع … من المال إلا مسحتا أو مجلف

MUQATIL:20:60-63/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:60-63/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:60-63/r2.claim: Moses warned them not to falsely claim that the hand and staff were not from God but were magic.

MUQATIL:20:60-63/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:60-63/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:60-63/r3.claim: Yashtikum means God will destroy them all with punishment; whoever invents a lie about God has lost.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r2.claim: He tells them not to falsely call God's signs and miracles sorcery.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r3.claim: Kufis other than Abū Bakr use the form yushitukum; the others have fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ. Both forms mean destroy or annihilate.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r3.anchor: كوفي غير أبي بكر يهلككم وبفتح الياء والحاء غيرهم والسحت والاسحاق بمعنى الإعدام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r4.claim: The verb is in the subjunctive as the result of the prohibition.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r4.anchor: وبفتح الياء والحاء غيرهم والسحت والاسحاق بمعنى الإعدام وانتصب على جواب النهى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p59#2/r5.claim: Whoever lies about God has failed.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r14.claim: Moses addressed both Pharaoh and the magicians.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r14.anchor: { قال لهم موسى } أي قال لفرعون والسحرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r15.claim: ويلكم is an invocation of woe and is treated as a verbal noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r15.anchor: { ويلكم } دعاء عليهم بالويل. وهو بمعنى المصدر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r16.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r16.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses ويلكم as an accusative meaning May God impose woe on them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r16.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: هو منصوب بمعنى ألزمهم الله ويلا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r17.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r17.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows it as a vocative, as in the phrase woe to us at 36:52.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r17.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: هو منصوب بمعنى ألزمهم الله ويلا. قال: ويجوز أن يكون نداء كقوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r18.claim: Moses tells them not to invent lies about God, associate partners with Him, or call the miracles magic.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r18.anchor: أي لا تختلقوا عليه الكذب، ولا تشركوا به، ولا تقولوا للمعجزات إنها سحر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r19.claim: The punishment will eradicate them by destruction; سحت and أسحت mean the same, the root originally suggesting complete removal of hair.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r19.anchor: أي يستأصلكم بالإهلاك. يقال فيه: سحت وأسحت بمعنى. وأصله من استقصاء الشعر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r20.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r20.claim: The Kufans read فيسحتكم from أسحت; other readers use سحت, with the two forms associated with Tamim and the Hijaz respectively.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r20.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «فيسحتكم» من أسحت، الباقون «فيسحتكم» من سحت وهذه لغة أهل الحجاز

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r21.claim: The verb is subjunctive as the consequence of the prohibition.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r22.speaker: الفرزدق
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r22.claim: Al-Farazdaq's verse witnesses the thorough-removal sense of مسحتا.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r22.anchor: وقال الفرزدق: وعض زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع من المال إلا مسحتا أو مجلف

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r23.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r23.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says riders continually argue over parsing al-Farazdaq's verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r23.anchor: الزمخشري: وهذا بيت لا تزال الركب تصطك في تسوية إعرابه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r24.claim: Whoever fabricates against God fails and perishes, losing mercy and reward by claiming what God did not authorize.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:60-61/r24.anchor: أي خسر وهلك، وخاب من الرحمة والثواب من ادعى على الله ما لم يأذن به

RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r14.claim: Moses warned them before the contest not to falsely claim that his message was untrue and sorcery, thereby licensing an attempt to oppose him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r14.anchor: قدم قبل كل شيء الوعيد والتحذير مما قالوه وأقدموا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r15.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows two parses of wailakum: an implicit verb meaning 'may God impose woe on you if you lie,' or a vocative, as in the cited verses.
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r15.anchor: قال الزجاج : يجوز في انتصاب ويلكم أن يكون المعنى ألزمهم الله ويلا

RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r16.claim: The phrase means that God will punish them with a destructive, annihilating punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r16.anchor: وقوله : { فيسحتكم بعذاب } أي يعذبكم عذابا مهلكا مستأصلا

RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r17.speaker: حمزة وعاصم والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r17.claim: Hamza, Asim, and al-Kisa'i read the yāʾ with ḍamma, using the form from isḥāt.
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r17.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وعاصم والكسائي برفع الياء من الإسحات والباقون بفتحها

RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r18.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r18.claim: The other readers use fatḥa on the yāʾ, reading the form from saḥt.
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r18.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وعاصم والكسائي برفع الياء من الإسحات والباقون بفتحها

RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r19.claim: Isḥāt is the dialect of Najd and Banu Tamim, while saḥt is the Hijazi form; both convey being destroyed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r19.anchor: والإسحات لغة أهل نجد وبني تميم والسحت لغة أهل الحجاز

RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r20.claim: Forging lies against God brings either annihilation in this world or severe punishment in the Hereafter, and also failure and deprivation of one's aim.
RAZI-FULL:v22p63#3/r20.anchor: من افترى على الله كذبا حصل له أمران

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r7.claim: Although the warning was given openly, the addressees were blinded inwardly to its significance, so Moses’ warning of punishment and promise of grace did not benefit them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r7.anchor: وأعماه عن شهود ذلك بسره ، فما نجع فيه كلامه ، وما انتفع بما حذره من انتقامه

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r8.claim: Moses called them to God and spoke of the afterlife’s reward and punishment, but they responded only in worldly terms; reminders increased their heedlessness and ignorance.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r8.anchor: دعاهم موسى إلى الله ، وخاطبهم في حديث الآخرة من تبشير بثواب ، وإنذار بعذاب

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r9.claim: One marked by divine exclusion lacks gnosis and faith, regrets nothing missed, and does not believe in what lies ahead.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r9.anchor: كذلك صفة من وسمه الحق بالإبعاد ، لم يكن له عرفان ، ولا بما يقال إيمان

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r12.claim: Moses exhausted admonition and gentleness, while Pharaoh displayed every form of folly and stupidity.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r12.anchor: ولم يدع موسى شيئا من الوعظ والرفق ، ولم يغادر فرعون شيئا من البله والحمق

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r13.claim: The sorcerers dismissed Moses’ warning as a lie and his miracle as magic, claiming that he and Aaron sought to expel them and destroy their exemplary way.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r13.anchor: فحملوا مقالته على الإفك ، ورموا معجزته بالسجر فقالوا

STUDYQURAN:20:61/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:61/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:61/r1.claim: In context, Moses warns them not to label God's signs and miracles sorcery.
STUDYQURAN:20:61/r1.anchor: In this context, Moses’ words Do not fabricate a lie against God mean,“Do not call God’s signs and miracles sorcery”

TAB-FULL:v16p94/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r1.claim: Moses warns the sorcerers not to invent lies against God or attribute false claims to Him.
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r1.anchor: فيستأصلكم بهلاك فيبيدكم. وللعرب فيه لغتان: سحت

TAB-FULL:v16p94/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r2.claim: Yasḥatukum means He will annihilate you; saḥata and asḥata are known forms, with saḥata more common, as al-Farazdaq's line illustrates.
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r2.anchor: وللعرب فيه لغتان: سحت، وأسحت، وسحت أكثر من أسحت، يقال منه: سحت الدهر، وأسحت مال فلان

TAB-FULL:v16p94/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the threat as He will destroy you.
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r3.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فيسحتكم بعذاب} [طه: 61] يقول: فيهلككم

TAB-FULL:v16p94/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r4.claim: Qatāda says the punishment cuts them off completely.
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {فيسحتكم بعذاب} [طه: 61] يقول: يستأصلكم بعذاب

TAB-FULL:v16p94/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd describes the destruction as total, leaving no remnant.
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فيسحتكم بعذاب} [طه: 61] قال: يهلككم هلاكا ليس فيه بقية

TAB-FULL:v16p94/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r6.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the phrase as destroying them with punishment.
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r6.anchor: عن السدي، {فيسحتكم بعذاب} [طه: 61] يقول يهلككم بعذاب

TAB-FULL:v16p94/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r7.claim: Medina, Basra, and some Kūfan readers use fatḥ from saḥata; most Kūfans use ḍamm from asḥata. Both are famous dialectal readings with the same meaning, and both correct; al-Ṭabarī prefers fatḥ as the more eloquent highland usage, while ḍamm is Najdi.
TAB-FULL:v16p94/r7.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء أهل المدينة والبصرة وبعض أهل الكوفة: (فيسحتكم) بفتح الياء من سحت يسحت. وقرأته عامة قراء الكوفة

TABATABAI:20:64/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r1.claim: The fabrication against God is belief in idolatry: gods have divinity and intercession, and world management returns to them.
TABATABAI:20:64/r1.anchor: المراد بافتراء الكذب على الله الاعتقاد باصول الوثنية كالوهية الآلهة وشفاعتها ورجوع تدبير العالم إليها

TABATABAI:20:64/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r2.claim: The warning of punishment follows from the prohibition: association with God brings annihilation for shirk; the indefinite punishment signals its severity.
TABATABAI:20:64/r2.anchor: وتنكير العذاب للدلالة على شدته وعظمته

TABATABAI:20:64/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r3.claim: Failure is despair at not attaining the hoped-for outcome; the statement is framed as a general principle because false causes cannot produce true, lasting good.
TABATABAI:20:64/r3.anchor: الخيبة اليأس من بلوغ النتيجة المأمولة وقد وضعت الجملة في الكلام وضع الأصل الكلي

TABATABAI:20:64/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r4.claim: This verse applies failure to fabrication in general, broader than the warning that those who fabricate against God do not prosper.
TABATABAI:20:64/r4.anchor: لإثباتها الخيبة في مطلق الإفتراء بخلاف الآية الثانية

TABATABAI:20:64/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r5.claim: The author points back to his discussion of the false blood on Joseph's shirt as another case showing that lies do not prosper.
TABATABAI:20:64/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم كلام في أن الكذب لا يفلح في ذيل قوله وجاؤا على قميصه بدم كذب

TABRISI:20:59-63/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:59-63/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:59-63/r6.claim: Saḥata and asḥata have the same sense, to destroy utterly; al-Farazdaq's line uses masḥatan for what has been wiped out.
TABRISI:20:59-63/r6.anchor: فإن سحت وأسحت بمعنى قال الفرزدق:

TABRISI:20:59-63/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:59-63/r7.speaker: الفرزدق
TABRISI:20:59-63/r7.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line witnesses the meaning “wiped out” for masḥatan.
TABRISI:20:59-63/r7.anchor:
قال الفرزدق:
وعض زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r7.claim: Waylakum is a warning and threat, meaning “may God impose woe and punishment on you.”
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r7.anchor: وهي كلمة وعيد وتهديد معناه ألزمكم الله الويل والعذاب

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r8.claim: Another analysis treats waylakum as a vocative invocation of woe; it may also be parsed as two words or an expression of wonder.
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن ويلكم كلمتان تقديرهما ويلكم فيكون مبتدأ وخبرا أو يكون ويلكم بمنزلة أتعجب لكم

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the warning as “do not associate anyone with God.”
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r9.anchor: لا تشركوا مع الله أحدا عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r10.claim: Alternatively, do not call God's miracles magic, present sorcery as truth, or claim Pharaoh is a deity to worship.
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r10.anchor: لا تكذبوا على الله بأن تنسبوا معجزاتي إلى السحر وسحركم إلى أنه حق

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r11.speaker: قتادة، السدي
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r11.claim: Qatādah and al-Suddī gloss yusḥitkum as “annihilate you.”
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r11.anchor: فيسحتكم } أي يستأصلكم { بعذاب } عن قتادة والسدي

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r12.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي، مقاتل، الجبائي
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Kalbī, Muqātil, and al-Jubbāʾī gloss it as “destroy you.”
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r12.anchor: وقيل: يهلككم عن ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل والجبائي

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r13.claim: The root denotes shaving something down completely; the verb then means to destroy or annihilate.
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r13.anchor: وأصل السحت إستقصاء الحلق يقال سحت شعره إذا استأصله

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r14.claim: Qatādah explains khāba as “he has lost.”
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r14.anchor: أي خسر من كذب على الله ونسب إليه باطلا عن قتادة

TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r15.claim: Another explanation says the fabricator has lost hope of God's reward and Paradise.
TABRISI:20:57-66#3/r15.anchor: انقطع رجاء من كذب على الله عن ثوابه وجنته

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r1.claim: Yusḥitukum means to destroy or eradicate; the verb is also said as saḥata or asḥata.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r1.anchor: فيسحتكم بعذاب} أي يهلككم ويستأصلكم. يقال: سحته الله وأسحته.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r2.claim: The one who fabricates has lied.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#2/r2.anchor: وقد خاب من افترى} أي كذب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r1.claim: Moses addresses the sorcerers whom Pharaoh gathered to defeat him; they are those referred to by the earlier statement that Pharaoh gathered his stratagem.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r1.anchor: قال لهم موسى} أي: للسحرة الذين جمعهم فرعون ليغلبوا موسى، وهم المعنيون بقوله: {فجمع كيده}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq analyzes waylakum either as an accusative phrase meaning God imposed woe on them or as a vocative, like “O woe to us” at 36:52.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (منصوب على ألزمهم الله ويلا. قال: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على النداء، كما قال: {يا ويلنا من بعثنا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning means not to associate anyone with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (لا تشركوا مع الله أحدا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r4.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r4.claim: Others say Moses warns them not to claim that the hand and staff are not signs from God, which would be a lie against Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: (لا تقولوا اليد والعصا ليستا آيتين من قبل الله فإنكم عند هذا القول تكذبون على الله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r5.claim: A variant reading pronounces the initial yāʾ of fayusḥitakum with ḍamma.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش والفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda, al-Akhfash, al-Farra, al-Zajjaj, and the linguists say saḥata and asḥata mean to eradicate or destroy completely.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r6.anchor: يقال: سحته وأسحته إذا استأصله وأهلكه (¬1)، قاله أبو عبيدة، والأخفش، والفراء، والزجاج، وجميع أهل اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r7.speaker: الفرزدق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r7.claim: A line by al-Farazdaq uses musḥatan for wealth left utterly depleted, illustrating the root’s sense of eradication.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r7.anchor: وعض زمان يا بن مروان لم يدع ... من المال إلا مسحتا أو مجلف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, in the al-Walibi report, glosses the threat as “He will destroy you,” a view shared by Mujahid, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي: ({فيسحتكم}: فيهلككم) (¬4). وهو قول مجاهد، ومقاتل، والكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r9.speaker: قتادة وأبان بن تغلب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r9.claim: Qatada and Aban ibn Taghlib gloss the word as “He will eradicate you.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r10.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r10.claim: In the report through ʿAta, Ibn Abbas says it means that God will wear them down with punishment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r11.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r11.claim: Al-Layth explains saḥatnāhum as bringing people to the utmost hardship and notes asḥatnāhum as a dialect form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r11.anchor: قال الليث: (يقال: سحتناهم بلغنا مجهودهم في المشقة عليهم. قال: وأسحتناهم لغة) (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r12.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r12.claim: The language scholars connect the root to close shaving and total removal; the verse’s point is that God’s punishment takes them all without exception.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p434/r12.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: (السحت في اللغة معناه: استقصى الحلق، يقال: سحت الشعر إذا استقصى حلقه، وسحت الحالق إذا استأصل،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the one who fails is whoever claims another god alongside God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (خيب (¬4) من ادعى مع الله إلها آخر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r2.claim: Qatada says the loser is whoever lies about God and attributes falsehood to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p436/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: (خسر من كذب على الله ونسب إليه باطلا)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:58-61/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:58-61/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:58-61/r5.claim: Moses told the sorcerers not to associate partners with God or God would eradicate them; a fabricator claims another deity alongside God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:58-61/r5.anchor: { لا تفتروا على الله كذبا } لا تشركوا مع الله أحدا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p265/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p265/r3.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p265/r3.claim: Al-Hasan explains yusḥitakum as “eradicate you” with punishment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p265/r3.anchor: حدثني الحسن بن دينار، عن الحسن قال: فيستأصلكم بعذاب

MAJAZ:v2p20/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p20/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p20/r5.claim: Yusḥitakum means destroy you; both saḥata and asḥata occur, and the cited lines by al-Farazdaq and Suwayd use the root for destruction or what remains.
MAJAZ:v2p20/r5.anchor: فيسحتكم بعذاب» (61) مجازه: فيهلكم، وفيه لغتان سحت الدهر والجدب بنى فلان، وقوم يقولون: أسحته بالألف

BAQILLANI:v1p91/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r1.claim: The cited poets use extreme praise, claiming that virtue reaches above the sun or sky and that even generous praise cannot match its subject.
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r1.anchor: وقول زهير ( لو كان يقعد فوق الشمس من كرم قوم بأولهم أو مجدهم قعدوا )

BAQILLANI:v1p91/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r2.claim: Some treat īghāl as a poetic device, sought in Qur'an only at verse endings; Imru al-Qays's rhyme heightens the description though its meaning stands without it.
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r2.anchor: فقد أوغل بالقافية في الوصف وأكد التشبيه بها والمعنى قد يستقل دونها

BAQILLANI:v1p91/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r4.claim: Returning the end of a composition to its beginning is a badiʿ device; 20:61 repeats the warning against fabrication, while 17:21 gives another example.
BAQILLANI:v1p91/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك رد عجز الكلام على صدره كقول الله عز وجل

ITQAN:v3p277/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p277/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p277/r1.claim: Taṣdīr, also called returning the ending to the beginning, repeats a word from the verse opening in its ending.
ITQAN:v3p277/r1.anchor: وأما التصدير فهو أن تكون تلك اللفظة بعينها تقدمت في أول الآية وتسمى أيضا رد العجز على الصدر

ITQAN:v3p277/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p277/r2.speaker: ابن المعتز
ITQAN:v3p277/r2.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz divides taṣdīr into three forms: the ending matches the last word, the first word, or another word in the verse’s opening.
ITQAN:v3p277/r2.anchor: وقال ابن المعتز هو ثلاثة أقسام الأول أن يوافق آخر الفاصلة آخر كلمة في الصدر

ITQAN:v3p277/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p277/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p277/r3.claim: The closing افترى returns to the earlier تفتروا, illustrating the form where the ending repeats part of the verse’s wording.
ITQAN:v3p277/r3.anchor: قال لهم موسى ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿ وقد خاب من افترى

BURHAN:v1p93/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p93/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p93/r4.claim: Taṣdīr is another kind of verse ending, illustrated by examples that echo wording or a root from the opening in the close.
BURHAN:v1p93/r4.anchor: الثانى التصدير كقوله تعالى ﴿ لا تفتروا على الله كذبا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r8.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم عن أبي بكر وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r8.claim: These readers fatḥa the yāʾ in فيسحتكم, from saḥata; Hafs, Hamza, and al-Kisāʾī use ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ, from asḥata.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r8.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ﴿ فيسحتكم ﴾ بفتح الياء من سحت

NASHR:v2p320/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p320/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص ورويس
NASHR:v2p320/r4.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Hafs, and Roways read فيسحتكم with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ; the others use fatḥa on both.
NASHR:v2p320/r4.anchor: فيسحتكم فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص ورويس بضم الياء
